about.title: Manhattan Beach Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Manhattan Beach residents rely on a mix of local clinics and larger Los Angeles County hospital systems for everything from routine checkups to emergency care. Most of the time that care goes fine, but when a provider misses a clear warning sign, operates on the wrong site, or mishandles medication, the consequences can follow a patient for years. California law does not treat every poor outcome as malpractice — the law requires proof that a provider fell below the accepted standard of care and that this failure caused real harm. Because these cases hinge on medical records, expert review, and strict filing deadlines, it helps to have someone experienced look at what occurred early on. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself; we simply connect Manhattan Beach patients and families with an independent attorney who can evaluate the medical chart, explain whether a case appears viable, and walk through next steps in plain language, at no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Manhattan Beach Patients Turn to LawProactive

items.title: MICRA Deadlines Are Strict
items.desc: California generally gives one year from when you discover the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself, plus a required 90-day notice before filing suit. Missing these windows can end a claim before it starts, so early review matters.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: California law requires a qualified medical expert to weigh in on whether a provider's conduct fell below the accepted standard of care. An independent attorney can help arrange that review rather than leaving you to interpret medical records alone.

items.title: Understanding the Non-Economic Damages Cap
items.desc: California places a statutory cap on non-economic damages in medical malpractice cases, and that cap adjusts upward each year under MICRA. A connected attorney can explain how this applies to your specific situation without promising any particular result.

items.question: Does a bad outcome from surgery or treatment automatically mean malpractice occurred?
items.answer: No. California law is clear that an unfavorable result alone doesn't establish malpractice. What matters is whether the provider's care fell below the accepted medical standard and whether that failure caused the harm. An independent attorney can help sort out whether your situation meets that bar.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in Manhattan Beach?
items.answer: Under MICRA, the general rule is one year from when you discover the injury, and no more than three years from when it happened, whichever comes first. There's also a required 90-day notice period before a lawsuit can be filed. Because these timelines are strict and fact-specific, it's worth getting a case reviewed sooner rather than later.

items.question: Is there a cost to have LawProactive connect me with an attorney in the Manhattan Beach area?
items.answer: There's no cost to you for the connection itself, and attorneys in our network generally work on contingency, meaning they're only paid if you recover compensation. We're not a law firm — we simply help Manhattan Beach residents reach an independent attorney who can evaluate their situation.
